rule: M1.2d rule (c), ruling D-19 (Mark, attended 2026-10-02): a component that Hipparcos lists separately from its CNS5 system row takes the CNS5 system row's parallax, at its own HIP2 position propagated to that row's epoch. It never takes its own HIP2 parallax. Read by sim/tools/bright.ail (parseOverrides); every row must apply exactly once or the bright tier is refused.

components.name: alpha Centauri B
components.system_cns5: 3627 (Gl 559 AB; CNS5 has no separate A/B rows)
components.why: HIP2 gives B 796.92 +- 25.90 mas (4.09 ly) against A 754.81 +- 4.11 mas (4.32 ly): taken at face value B sits 0.23 ly in front of A, for a pair about 23 AU apart (plan finding F2).
components.citation: van Leeuwen 2007, A&A 474, 653 (Hipparcos new reduction, VizieR I/311: HIP 71681 and 71683); Golovin et al. 2023, A&A 670, A19 (CNS5, VizieR J/A+A/670/A19: CNS5 3627, parallax 754.81 mas from van Leeuwen 2007); Kervella et al. 2016, A&A 594, A107 (747.17 mas for the pair; not used, D-19 keeps the catalogue's own number).
